newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 31.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Overall trading was cautious but the correction anticipated by many buyers failed to develop through Thursday, Random Lengths said in its end-week update. Prices finished mixed but on balance the framing index was higher. Western S-P-F was slightly softer but green Douglas fir rallied sharply.
Southern Pine prices ended mixed, with the narrows flat to soft and the wides tight; buyers fielded fewer end-of-month offers from mills than they had hoped, Random Lengths said.

Traders said weather remained a key factor in sales. Where winter loosened its grip, as it did in areas of the Northeast and California, trading picked up. On the other hand, mills that depend on the Upper Midwest for business found sales slow.

Some retailers said they would have to move already-sold wood bottled up in their yards by weather in order to make room for new purchases. Stocking distributors, treaters, and large retail chains continued to buy on a just-in-time basis.
Wholesalers took a cautious approach in most species, often finding little room between firm mill prices and dealers looking for price concessions, Random Lengths said.

Winter delayed some rail shipments, notably from eastern Canada. The U.S.-Canada lumber agreement remained on the back burner but as many mills in eastern Canada edged closer to the $100 fee threshold, their customers wondered how they would react. Canadian exports as of Jan 22 totalled 24.1 percent of Jan-March quota and 85 percent of annual April/March quota.
Wide widths of dimension showed more strength than narrows but rising prices prompted talk of competition for I-joists.
Long lengths were strong in a number of species and boards remained tight in the key 1x12 items, Random Lengths said.
